## Live confirmation, 2026-11-22 17:12 PST (read-only /proc inspection)

The review-bot container restarted at 16:20:22 PST (deploy of springbok's 4bf065d8ac4; this ticket's fix is not deployed yet). The stall repeated: Ifd689bf timed out at 16:45:02 and I5e44129b (Gerrit 3526, this ticket's own change) at 17:05:03, both with no log after `merge_detection`.

At 17:11:58 PST, 51.6 minutes after the restart:
- `/proc/locks`: `bytes.total.lock` (inode 8388737, the snapshot store's accounting lock) is held by the review-bot process (pid 1254853), and 3 more requests from the same pid wait on it.
- Threads of that pid: 3 in `locks_lock_inode_wait` (blocked on a flock), 1 in `xfs_buf_lock` (the sweep reading disk), 7 in futex waits, 1 in epoll.
- `fetch.lock` has no holder or waiter, which rules out the fetch lock as the wait.

This is the mechanism from the investigation, observed directly: the in-process janitor's startup sweep holds the accounting lock while review threads queue on it.

Adjacent finding: the bot process has 17 `[git] <defunct>` zombie children (ages 0-47 min). The review-bot runs as the container's PID 1 and does not reap orphaned grandchildren. Filed separately; it is not the stall.
